properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 3:54PM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 348 PM AKDT, The river gauge at the Yentna River at Lake
Creek indicates rises in water levels from heavy rain across
the warned area. Flooding is ongoing. Trees and debris larger
than telephone poles have been observed flowing down the
river. Between 1.0 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible
with higher amounts possible in the upper Yentna Basin.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 7:51am the stage was 20.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest slightly above 22 feet late tonight and
into early Wednesday morning.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

properties.headline: Dust Storm Warning issued August 4 at 5:57PM MST until August 4 at 7:30PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Dust Storm Warning for...
Northeastern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 730 PM MST.

* At 557 PM MST, a wall of dust was located along a line from 11
miles northeast of Willcox to 17 miles north of Portal, moving
southwest at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Less than a quarter mile visibility.

SOURCE...Detected by National Weather Service meteorologists.

IMPACT...Dangerous life-threatening travel.

* Locations impacted include...
Willcox, Bowie, Dragoon, Chiricahua National Monument,
Pearce-Sunsites, Cochise, Sunizona, Kansas Settlement and San
Simon.

This includes the following highways...
Route 181 between mile markers 39 and 64. Route 191 between mile
markers 27 and 91. Interstate 10 between mile markers 322 and 390.
Route 186 between mile markers 327 and 359.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not drive into a dust storm. PULL ASIDE STAY ALIVE!

Dust storms lead to dangerous driving conditions with visibility
reduced to near zero. If driving, avoid dust storms if possible. If
caught in one, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep your
foot off the brake.

There is no safe place on a highway when a dust storm hits.
Visibility can be lost immediately, making it difficult or impossible
to slow down and avoid stopped vehicles. Delay travel, or safely exit
the highway before the dust storm arrives.

CMAMtext: NWS: DUST STORM WARNING til 7:30 PM MST. Be ready for a sudden drop to zero visibility.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: DUST STORM WARNING for this area until 7:30 PM MST. Be ready for sudden drop to zero visibility. Pull Aside, Stay Alive! When visibility drops, pull far off the road and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights off and keep your foot off the brake. Infants, the elderly and those with respiratory issues urged to take precautions.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 8:07PM CDT until August 6 at 8:10PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 32.0 feet, The Nueces River backs up minor creeks to
near the slab elevation of homes in the River Creek Acres
Subdivision, five miles southeast of George West. Livestock are cut
off and could drown in low areas of the flood plain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 33.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 9.0 feet Sunday evening.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
